Eurovision trivia — sample questions and how to play live

Eurovision trivia is a question-and-answer format about the history, voting, and winners of the Eurovision Song Contest. In Eurovision Games, trivia is the duel mechanic: any two players can challenge each other to a head-to-head 3-question round during the broadcast, and the winner steals their duel score from the loser or doubles it.

What is Eurovision trivia?

The Eurovision Song Contest has been running since 1956, with 50+ countries competing across 70 grand finals (1956-2026; 2020 cancelled) — that's a deep well of trivia. Categories that come up most: winners by year, voting milestones, language rules, scoring changes, country debuts and withdrawals, viral entries, controversies, and song titles.

Sample questions (with answers)

Ten questions pulled from the live bank — try them before you challenge a friend.

  1. Q1.Which country has won Eurovision the most times?

    • Sweden
    • Ireland
    • United Kingdom
    • France

    Answer: The record is 7 wins, held by Ireland and Sweden.

  2. Q2.In what year did ABBA win Eurovision?

    • 1972
    • 1974
    • 1976
    • 1980

    Answer: 1974, with "Waterloo" representing Sweden.

  3. Q3.Which city hosts Eurovision 2026?

    • Stockholm
    • Vienna
    • Liverpool
    • Madrid

    Answer: Vienna, Austria.

  4. Q4.What does the "douze points" award?

    • 10 points
    • 12 points
    • 8 points
    • 7 points

    Answer: 12 points — the highest score a jury or country can give in a single vote.

  5. Q5.Which country has competed the most times without winning?

    • Cyprus
    • Iceland
    • Malta
    • Bulgaria

    Answer: Cyprus: 42 contests without a win.

  6. Q6.What was Conchita Wurst’s winning song in 2014?

    • Heroes
    • Rise Like a Phoenix
    • Euphoria
    • Toy

    Answer: Rise Like a Phoenix (Austria, 2014).

  7. Q7.Which country withdrew from Eurovision after winning multiple early contests, then returned in 2011?

    • Italy
    • Monaco
    • Yugoslavia
    • Luxembourg

    Answer: Italy — winners in 1964 and 1990, withdrew after 1997, returned in 2011.

  8. Q8.How many points did Loreen score with "Tattoo" in 2023?

    • 340
    • 440
    • 583
    • 628

    Answer: 583 — winning Sweden its 7th title.

  9. Q9.What is the maximum number of points a country can earn in the modern voting system?

    • 400
    • 600
    • 758
    • No fixed maximum

    Answer: No fixed maximum. Every other voting country can give up to 12 jury points and 12 televote points, plus 12 from the Rest of the World vote, so the ceiling depends on how many countries take part. The record is 758 (Salvador Sobral, Portugal 2017).

  10. Q10.In what year was public televoting first used at Eurovision?

    • 1991
    • 1997
    • 2001
    • 2009

    Answer: 1997 — five countries trialled televoting, and from 1998 most countries used it.

Questions are drawn from a curated bank and have not been individually fact-checked. This is a party game for fun — treat answers as entertainment.

Categories and difficulty tiers

  • Easy: winners by country, the douze points rule, host city.
  • Medium: song titles, year-of-debut, semi-final placements.
  • Hard: voting reform years, withdrawals, controversies, language rules.

How duels work in Eurovision Games

Click any other player's name in the live leaderboard, hit Challenge, and a 3-question duel pops up on both your screens. Each player has 12 seconds per question, and each correct answer scores 12 minus the elapsed whole seconds. The higher total wins; equal totals are a tie with no winner. The winner steals their duel score from the loser or doubles it. Each of you can challenge the other once, plus one rematch for the loser, so you can’t farm one weaker opponent.

For the full duel rule book — scoring math, Steal vs Double, and the Duelist/Thief trophies — see the dedicated duels page.

Play live

Trivia happens during the show. Best windows: between underwhelming entries, during the interval act, and through the jury vote. Create a room on Eurovision Games and invite up to 19 friends to play.
